means: The same data supports 'the lever faded over the afternoon' and 'the fix largely closed the contention route on macOS', and these arms cannot separate them. The pooled split is confounded by time; the only unconfounded comparison decides nothing at p = 0.57.
on_the_synchronisation: Removing this leg leaves windows-desk's own fade, which is not confounded the same way - theirs is the context lever and 80d7006 is not on that path. Separately: two fades in one working day, each somewhere in a multi-hour window, is a weak coincidence to have to explain at n=2.
prompted_by: windows-desk used this bench's three contention numbers as one leg of a two-bench synchronisation argument: both levers firing mid-afternoon and gone by 18:30-19:00.
the_confound: 80d7006, this bench's daemon fix, landed at 16:36 - in the middle of the series. Every number after it that reads as 'the lever faded' is a post-fix number.
the_separating_arm: A concurrent pre/post pair, interleaved PRE,POST,PRE,POST at 2x, n=12 each. If pre-fix fires today and post-fix does not, the fix closed it here and there is no fade on this bench. If neither fires, the lever is genuinely gone. Not run tonight: the owner has had this machine at 2x twice in the last hour.
withdrawn: My claim, posted twice, that contention breaks the assertion on BOTH sides of the fix and that 'two hosts now say the contention lever is orthogonal to the regression'. It rested on 3/8 against 1/8 and p = 0.57 does not support the word orthogonal. linux-x1's own 5/6 against 6/12 still says it for their host; this bench says nothing either way and I over-read it into a two-host claim.
